You should:

be aware of common conditions that individuals might have within adult social care and how you can support them in the context of your role. This might include:

adults with learning disabilities

autistic adults

people living with mental health or dementia

dysphagia and other conditions that can impact someone’s ability to swallow safely

diabetes, allergies and other medical dietary requirements

appetite and hydration challenges in older adults

understand how good nutrition and hydration help health and wellbeing and help prevent malnutrition and dehydration

have an awareness of common medical terms used within the health and social care sector

be able to speak with confidence when communicating with other professionals, including from the health service and local council

Understanding compliance and safety for catering in adult care

You should understand and follow:

the relevant food hygiene standards

health and safety and control of substances hazardous to health (COSHH) regulations as they relate to your role

hazard analysis and critical control point (HACCP) principles and temperature control regulations

Care Quality Commission regulations relevant to catering in care settings

Food hygiene for people who serve food and drink

You should:

understand the principles of food safety

understand the importance of food safety measures when providing food and drink for individuals

be able to maintain hygiene when handling food and drink

be able to meet safety requirements when serving food and drink for individuals

be able to meet safety requirements when clearing away food and drink

Provide catering in adult social care

You should:

understand food preparation frameworks and principles that are used in adult social care. This will include:

the Food First approach

the International Dysphagia Diet Standardisation Initiative (IDDSI)

the Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST)

understand why individuals in adult social care environments might refuse food or drink

understand how to prompt and encourage food and drink intake

understand how medications can impact how food and drink should be provided and be able to manage around these requirements

be able to prepare meals and drinks managing individuals’ personal conditions such as diabetes or allergies or where modified texture diets are required

be able to support monitoring individuals’ weight, modifying meals when issues are noted

be able to prepare food and drink safely in adult social care environments

Engaging with IT systems

You should:

be able to record catering tasks completed in IT systems as directed by your organisation

be able to keep up-to-date and accurate records of catering completed in your setting

where applicable, be able to track budgets for catering through systems agreed with your employer

Understanding person-centred meal planning and preparation

You should:

understand what is meant by the term ‘person-centred care’

be able to meal plan in a person-centred way, meeting individual preferences and needs

be able to meet cultural and religious considerations in meal planning

be able to liaise with dietitians, other health professionals, care staff and people who draw on care and support to ensure that meal planning and provision is person-centred

be able to absorb feedback from people who draw on care and support, helping shape meal planning and dining experiences

be able to positively engage with people who draw on care and support during mealtimes, supporting them to have a positive and inclusive dining experience

Support wellbeing through catering in care environments

You should:

where appropriate, be able to work with activity co-ordinators to organise specific food events and activities for the benefit of people who draw on care and support

where appropriate and safe, be able to support residents to build their own independence and confidence in making food for themselves

be able to support the health and wellbeing of people who draw on care and support

Infection prevention and control

You should:

understand the importance of infection prevention and control in care settings

understand what cleaning products are safe to be used in a kitchen environment to help prevent and control the spread of infection

know how to and be able to prevent and control the spread of infection

be able to support managing outbreaks in care environments

Additional knowledge and skills

In addition to the above knowledge and skills, catering staff should also have the following competencies that align with the knowledge and skills detailed in the ‘New to care’ role category (as required):

using and managing data, and data security

reduce the likelihood of abuse

demonstrating effective interpersonal skills

managing your time

introduction to health, safety​ and wellbeing

fire safety (health and safety)

Oliver’s Training

Complete Oliver’s Training on Learning Disability and Autism: Tier 1. Tier 2 can be undertaken in settings providing direct care to individuals with autism or a learning disability.
